source.read_from: zip members in place, nothing extracted or executed

method.model: One ridge logistic per subject and label, one-vs-rest, on 33 AU amplitudes plus centred face gender. Intercept and gender unpenalised.
method.ci: 95 percent percentile, resampling subjects within stimulus set. Conditional on the fixed stimulus set; see beta_se_stimulus in the CSV.
method.beta_units: log odds per unit amplitude (0 to 1); composites are L plus R
method.do_effect: Difference in P(label) for do(AU=1) minus do(AU=0), others at observed values, averaged over the subject's trials. One-vs-rest probabilities are renormalised over labels per trial, so effects sum to zero across labels. do(AU=1) is full amplitude, at the top of the tested range.
method.ceiling: family_25 is the recommended basis. Use the same-stimuli ceiling if a model sees these configurations; use the subjects_and_stimuli ceiling if it sees others. Keep beta and do_effect separate.

data_caveats: Conversational data have 20 subjects per group, not 60. The zip holds 60 TSVs per group, of which 40 are header-only, an artefact of a range(1, 61) loop in Snoek's split script.

Stimuli were randomised once, then shared. Every subject in a set saw the same configuration-plus-face stimuli, and row order is identical across subjects, so trial order is not available. Subject bootstrap CIs are conditional on that set.
Western basic is two cohorts: subjects 01-15 saw blended identities (959 face codes) and subjects 16-60 saw 8 base faces. Their configurations share 3 strings.
East Asian basic and conversational use nearly the same configurations. Western basic and conversational do not. See shared_au_configurations_between_datasets.

The 33 columns are recoded from 42 raw AUs: bilateral AUs become L and R together, and compounds AU1-2, AU25-12 and AU12-6 become their parts, taking the maximum. So AU columns are correlated by construction (up to r 0.79) and estimates assume additivity.
AU02R has no unilateral condition: it is active only for bilateral AU2. Read AU02L and AU02R through AU02_bilateral.

Column amplitudes are rounded to one decimal. The EA and conversational sixths (0.16, 0.33, 0.5, 0.66, 0.83, 1) survive in the row-label strings; Western basic labels were rebuilt after rounding. The thesis says steps of 0.25, which the files do not show.
Temporal parameters were randomised but are absent, so effects are averaged over time course and say nothing about dynamics. Effects hold for GFG faces in this design.
sub_split and trial_split were not used for estimation. They were built for Snoek's prediction models, and trial_split is unbalanced.
face_id 1-4 repeats across genders in the conversational files, so a face is gender plus id.
Subject 43EA has 783 trials; 01-60 all carry equal weight in the group mean.
Ridge shrinks magnitudes, and more so where a larger lambda was selected (see slope_selected_on_lowest_lambda). Compare patterns, not sizes, across tasks.

trial_count_reconciliation.notes_claim: 119,387 (own count) versus 121,902 (thesis) for Western basic, excluding 'other'
trial_count_reconciliation.design_rows: 60 subjects x 2400 trials = 144,000 (thesis and Snoek preprocessing code)
trial_count_reconciliation.conclusion: Likely but not proven. Snoek's determine_train_and_test.py drops from the test split every row whose configuration also occurs in train, then rewrites the subject TSVs. That explains why public subjects have 2342 or 2368 rows, not 2400. If the thesis count was taken before that step, the 3,090 dropped rows must hold 575 'other' responses, 18.6 percent against a 15.3 percent base rate, and the mean per subject fits. The raw .mat files are not public, so this cannot be confirmed. The removal depends on the stimulus, not the response, so it should not bias AU effects.
